PullRequest.Title: agentHost: offer skills of runtime plugins waiting for session start
PullRequest.Body:
## Why

Typing `/pot` in an idle Agents session did not offer `/pstack:poteto-mode`, even though the `pstack` plugin is installed and enabled. This affects skills from every installed Copilot plugin until the session's SDK runtime starts.

The host publishes a runtime plugin whose session has not started as `load: loading`, `effectiveEnabled` missing, and `enablement: [{ global, enabled: false }]`. That `false` is a deliberate fail-closed placeholder, and the plugin list shows the same state as "Waiting for Session Start". `getSkillCustomizations` read the placeholder as a real decision. So `AgentHostSkillCompletionProvider` and `CopilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider` dropped every skill of the plugin.

## What changed

- `isSkillContainerEnabled` in `customizationEnablement.ts` decides whether a container's skills can be used. A runtime plugin that is still waiting for session start uses the user's intended enablement, `managedDesiredEnabled ?? repositoryEnabled ?? globalEnabled`. Every other container keeps its published decision.
- `getSkillCustomizations` and the cached MCP-skill lookup in `AgentHostSkillCompletionProvider` use the helper.

## Tradeoffs

- The host's published `enabled: false` stays as it is. Changing it would turn pending plugins on for every consumer, including the SDK handoff, which must fail closed.
- A plugin whose runtime cannot be read (`load: error`) and a plugin whose runtime has decided (`effectiveEnabled` set) keep their published decision.

## Blast Radius

- Slash completions and runtime-command de-duplication now include skills of pending plugins the user intends to use.
- The customizations list can show MCP-server skill rows of a pending plugin once that server reports skills, matching how it already shows the pending plugin.
- While a session is pending, the host does not read repository plugin settings. A plugin disabled only for the repository can still be offered. Choosing it sends the slash text, and the started session loads plugins with their real enablement.

## Verification

- New unit test in `agentHostSkillCompletionProvider.test.ts`. It failed before the fix (only the settled plugin's skill appeared) and passes after it.
- `./scripts/test.sh` over the skill and slash completion providers, the enablement gate, `copilotAgent`, `agentService`, the customization item provider, the workbench customization service and harness, and plugin actions: 2792 passing, 0 failing, rerun after rebasing onto `main` with #349540.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check`, and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files pass.
- Replayed the customizations a real idle session published (from a local AHP transport log) through the compiled provider. Before: `/poteto` returned `[]`. After: `/poteto` returned `/pstack:poteto-help`, `/pstack:poteto-mode`, and three principle skills.
- Reproduced in a running Code OSS Agents window, then verified the fix in the same scenario. I created a session in a folder, switched sessions so it was evicted (`VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_SESSION_RESIDENCY_LIMIT=1`), deleted the folder, and reopened the session. Restore fell back to persisted history without starting the runtime, and `pstack` was published as `load: loading`, `enabled: false`, with no `effectiveEnabled`. That is the same state as the original report.
  - Without the fix, `/pot` completions returned only `/autopilot` and `/autopilot on`.
  - With the fix, `/pot` returned `/pstack:poteto-help`, `/pstack:poteto-mode`, and other `pstack` skills, while `pstack` stayed pending.
- A new session and a restored session whose runtime resumed still offer `/pstack:poteto-mode` for `/pot`.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed enablement gate, parsed pending MCP declarations, one-read-per-request grouping, immediate reference disposal, repeated connection setup without a resident runtime, and completion critical path are traced in code. Exact storage latency and how many installations declare MCP servers are unmeasured; other eligible undiscovered servers or an independently held DB reference can reduce the incremental cost.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SQLite connections, filesystem mkdir/statfs or realpath calls, journal/schema setup queries, metadata reads, and full-cache JSON parsing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One cache read per completion request, shared across all eligible servers—not one per server. Sequential requests after the previous reference is released reopen the database when no runtime or other consumer holds it; overlapping requests share connection initialization but still issue separate metadata reads and parse the entire cache. Parsing scales with all cached skill entries, including unrelated servers.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated filesystem/database initialization delays slash suggestions and all other completion-provider results, with additional I/O and parsing work while typing.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: For the same session with no other eligible undiscovered MCP servers, the published-disabled pending plugins were excluded and no MCP-cache database read/open occurred. Existing top-level or settled-plugin fallback reads are not the regression being reported.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Slash completion requests in an unstarted session with only pending-plugin MCP declarations now read the session database on every request, even when the cache is absent or the typed slash matches only a local skill.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The replaced gate at line 103 now calls isSkillContainerEnabled, which returns the intended enablement for Loading runtime plugins without effectiveEnabled. Previously their published enablement was false, so their MCP children could not make undiscoveredServers nonempty. With an enabled pending plugin containing an undiscovered MCP server, the changed gate now reaches the awaited readMcpSkillCache at line 111.
Findings.Title: Reuse the database across pending-plugin completion requests
Findings.Impact: In a new or restored session whose runtime has not started, an installed enabled plugin declaring an MCP server with children undefined now causes every slash-prefix update to await database access. With no resident session holding the database warm, even an empty cache repeatedly incurs connection and filesystem setup; slow or network-backed profile storage makes suggestions noticeably slower.
Findings.Evidence: CopilotAgent._readRuntimePlugins (12863–12881) publishes parsed MCP declarations under Loading plugins with effectiveEnabled absent and enabled:false. makeMcpServerCustomization (pluginParsers.ts:451–459) leaves children undefined, and resolveCustomizationEnablement resolves child enablement independently of the pending parent. _getCandidates gathers all such servers then awaits one readMcpSkillCache before returning even the already-built local candidates. readMcpSkillCache (shared/mcpSkillCache.ts:58–69) acquires and immediately disposes a DB reference on every call, with no positive, negative, or in-flight read cache. SessionDataService destroys the database at the last release (41–54); SessionDatabase._ensureDb (686–715) performs mkdir, SQLite open, journal configuration and migration checks, and getMetadata (1399–1402) then queries SQLite. CopilotAgentSession normally keeps a reference warm (2714–2715), but that owner is absent before runtime creation. AgentHostInputCompletionsBase returns incomplete:true (109), causing subsequent prefix updates to request completions again; cancellation is not forwarded across IPC (agentHostSessionHandler.ts:1769–1772). AgentHostCompletions awaits all providers (143–145), so this new await delays the combined response. This is static call-path evidence, not a measured benchmark.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a bounded session-keyed database lease across an active completion sequence, releasing it on idle/session teardown/provider disposal, rather than reopening it for each pending-plugin request. Preserve the existing latest-cache semantics and coalesce simultaneous reads for the same storage resource.

Scenarios.Scenario: Slash suggestions and runtime-command deduplication for an idle session with published pending-plugin skills but no eligible undiscovered MCP servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench awaits the completion IPC response. The host resolves the default chat/storage resource, reads the published customization snapshot, builds and filters skill candidates, and awaits all matching providers. The Copilot provider queries its existing runtime command catalog in parallel with known-skill enumeration. The new helper itself only validates a small metadata record; it does not start the runtime or discover plugin contents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request completions from the agent host and receive serialized items
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request/response per completion invocation; result bytes grow with matched deduplicated skills
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same IPC request count; pending-plugin skill items were excluded
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suggestions await the combined host response

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the catalog snapshot if default-chat storage is not already known
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when ownership/state knows storage; one catalog snapshot lookup otherwise

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing SDK rpc.commands.list for a cold runtime command catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per catalog miss after in-flight coalescing; zero on a warm catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical catalog query, caching, coalescing, and wait budget
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider waits up to its existing completion wait budget; command discovery can continue after that timeout

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P installed containers and S published skills; enumeration remains O(P+S). Generic completion deduplicates matching skills by slash name plus description, and the Copilot provider builds known/ineligible name sets. Newly eligible skill output scales with the intended visible skill count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion providers run concurrently via Promise.allSettled. Within the Copilot provider, catalog lookup and known-skill construction run concurrently. Catalog misses join one in-flight request; no new subprocess or runtime launch is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Published customizations avoid resolving the agent's customization inventory. Runtime command catalogs have positive caching and in-flight joining; invalidation discards the catalog and failures permit retry. Default-chat storage uses known ownership/state when available. The metadata helper does bounded object validation/allocation per pending container, not per skill.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the helper adds only bounded metadata handling and intended output on this path, without a new runtime/discovery boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number and description size of installed skills are unmeasured. Additional requested output is not independently a performance bug.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for direct published skill enumeration or deduplication; the additional work represents the requested skill visibility.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repeated slash-prefix updates before runtime start when the only eligible undiscovered MCP declarations belong to intended-enabled pending plugins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new container gate makes undiscoveredServers nonempty. _getCandidates awaits one readMcpSkillCache before returning even its already-built local candidates. AgentHostCompletions awaits all providers, so database access delays the entire suggestion response. Workbench cancellation is not forwarded to the host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the session SQLite database and SELECT the mcpSkills metadata value
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata query per completion request for the entire server group. One fresh connection per separated request when no other reference survives; overlapping requests share initialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero MCP-cache reads for the same pending-plugin-only scenario because the published-disabled parent gate excluded these servers. If another eligible undiscovered server already existed, this grouped read already occurred and the boundary count is unchanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before returning local and cached skill candidates; therefore blocks combined completion results

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: mkdir, SQLite file open, filesystem-locality check (Linux statfs or Windows realpath), journal configuration and schema-version checks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization sequence per cold connection; not per MCP server. Existing DBs still perform connection setup and migration checks; only actually pending migrations execute migration SQL
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No MCP-cache-driven connection initialization on this pending-plugin-only completion path
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the metadata query can return

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.parse the complete metadata value, build a map, validate cached skill records and parse their URIs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-cache parse per successful read, O(C) entries and metadata bytes, including unrelated cached servers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cache parse for this pending-plugin-only scenario; parsing for already-eligible top-level/settled-plugin fallback was pre-existing
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before filtering slash suggestions and before releasing the awaited provider response

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per completion invocation; incomplete completion lists cause subsequent prefix updates to invoke the provider again
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same IPC and cancellation behavior, but no pending-plugin MCP database work behind it
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client waits for host response; cancelled client results are dropped only afterward

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R completion requests while typing a slash token, U eligible undiscovered server names, and C entries across the full persisted MCP cache. There is one read for all U servers per request, not U reads. JSON parsing validates all C entries before selecting skills by server name.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Servers are grouped into one cache read. Overlapping requests can share the reference-counted DB and its initialization promise, but each still queries/parses independently; separated requests can each reopen. Providers run concurrently, yet the aggregate response waits for the slowest provider. No per-server process or network fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: readMcpSkillCache has no retained positive/negative result or in-flight read cache. Each call acquires/releases a database reference and parses the returned JSON, including an absent or empty result. Without a resident runtime or another reference owner, the last release destroys the DB wrapper, so a subsequent request is cold again. A resident CopilotAgentSession normally owns a warm reference, but that owner is absent in the reviewed pre-runtime scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced parsed declarations have children undefined, pending parent metadata changes the gate, child enablement is independently resolved, reads are grouped once per request, immediate reference release permits repeated cold opens, and the await blocks combined suggestions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage latency, cache size, installation prevalence, and independent reference holders are unmeasured. Network-backed or antivirus-scanned profiles increase the impact; an already eligible server or independently warm database reduces incremental cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity cache-lifecycle regression anchored to the changed gate at agentHostSkillCompletionProvider.ts:103. No separate per-server fan-out or concurrency-burst finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Skill completions after runtime enablement settles, for disabled/error plugins, and when no customization snapshot has yet been published
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Settled or error containers retain the prior published enablement decision. If published state is absent, generic completions still await agent.getChatCustomizations; Copilot's fallback awaits anchor discovery, outstanding synchronization, MCP discovery refresh and runtime plugin inventory before enumeration. This fallback sequencing predates the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read installed plugin inventory through the existing installedPlugins callback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory snapshot per sequenced runtime-plugin refresh, serving all installations; not one inventory request per skill
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical inventory refresh and settlement placement
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only on the unchanged absent-published-snapshot/refresh path, not the normal published-state keystroke path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve anchor paths and discover/parse plugin and MCP configuration contents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing anchor/discovery work plus a plugin parse per resource/version/content-revision cache miss; warm parsed plugin content is reused
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same discovery and parsed-content ownership; the new helper does not invoke these operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required by the existing customization-resolution fallback before skill enumeration

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing persisted MCP fallback for enabled settled/top-level servers with undefined children
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped read per completion invocation if any such server exists; zero when all relevant children are defined
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same boundary count and placement for settled/top-level servers

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugins grouped by resource/version for parsed content, active anchor sets and discovered skills. Cache fallback remains one MCP metadata read per request when at least one previously eligible server has undefined children; defined empty children suppress fallback.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing customization settlement awaits host/client synchronization, anchor/MCP discovery and runtime inventory concurrently. Runtime-plugin refresh uses a sequencer; installed plugin content parsing uses Promise.all and resource/version caches. Completion providers retain their existing parallel execution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime plugin parsed contents are cached by resource, version and content revision, with watcher invalidation. Published state bypasses discovery; absent published state uses the existing settled-resolution path. Loaded/disabled/error containers preserve prior decisions. Live MCP children, including empty arrays, suppress persisted fallback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that these decisions and boundary placements are unchanged; the diff's meaningful scheduling expansion is confined to pending intended-enabled containers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing discovery/cache-read durations are not measured. No PR-attributable frequency increase was found in this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. This PR corrects pending skill visibility, not a demonstrable removed performance regression, so no regression-fix provenance signal was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the customization list with published MCP skill children and rebuilding transcript customization indexes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The list first resolves runtime plugin inventory, expands plugin files, then enumerates published MCP skill rows. Newly eligible pending-plugin MCP skills become in-memory items; their resource contents are not read by this loop. Transcript CustomizationIndex ignores containerEnabled and continues indexing the same published children, with no new expensive boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: listPluginInstallations for each distinct runtime provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one inventory call per distinct provider for each list resolution, serving all that provider's plugins
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider grouping and inventory requests before getSkillCustomizations
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: List construction awaits inventories before expansion and row enumeration

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve agents/skills/commands/rules directories through the file service and read supported file metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four canonical-directory resolves per uncached plugin, additional bundle namespace resolves where applicable, and metadata reads for eligible skill/regular files. Warm URI/nonce/label expansion entries perform zero expansion filesystem calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All plugins were already expanded regardless of published enablement; the new MCP enablement result does not change expansion count
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing Promise.all expansion must finish before final list construction

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read eligible custom-agent files to derive hook rows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per eligible agent item when the existing hook-listing option is enabled; newly added MCP skill items are not agents and do not increase this count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same agent filtering and read count
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing optional hook enrichment before list return

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P plugins, Q distinct runtime providers, F supported plugin files and M published MCP skill children. Inventory is grouped by Q, directory expansion by plugin URI, and MCP rows by skill id. Existing parent lookup per MCP skill scans customizations; this cost is not a newly introduced algorithm.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runtime inventories are fetched with Promise.all across distinct providers. Uncached plugin expansions run concurrently, each resolving four canonical directories in parallel and reading metadata in per-folder batches. New MCP row construction is synchronous and does not schedule MCP network/resource reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin expansion caches children by plugin URI, nonce and label; unchanged entries skip filesystem expansion. Runtime inventory resolution is grouped by provider rather than plugin. Transcript indexes retain their existing path-cache reuse. New enablement metadata handling does not enlarge persistent index maps or retain resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed generator result only affects in-memory MCP row eligibility; plugin expansion and hook reads are already present and unaffected. The transcript index does not consume the changed boolean.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin/file/MCP skill counts and rendered-list costs are unmeasured. Metadata eligibility alone does not establish changed filesystem fan-out, forced layout, or retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence additional regression; did not report pre-existing scanning, parent lookup or renderer optimization opportunities.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete three-file inventory and every diff page in one performance-review pass. Traced completion callers, MCP cache and SQLite lifecycle, runtime plugin publication/child enablement, SDK command-catalog caching, customization list expansion, and transcript indexing. Submitted one concrete new pending-plugin completion cache-lifecycle finding; all other changed behavior adds bounded metadata handling or intended skill output without independently established regression. Static read-only review; no execution or profiling. The performance guide was requested but tool output exposed only a preview because of its size; learned-regression guidance and loaded skill evidence standards were available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
